problem_type: staged media verification lifecycle and immutable decoder boundary regression
symptom: A disabled ComfyUI workflow candidate could not be tested through the normal runtime, edits could delete active mappings before verification, mutable temporary paths were used by media probes, GLB references were only shallowly checked, and failed cleanup or cross-origin redirects could leave unsafe residual state.
direct_cause: ComfyUI import, runtime execution, media certification, asset persistence, cleanup recovery, custom-call transport, and redirect handling did not all share the same candidate lease, immutable-byte, bounded-process, and sanitized-evidence contracts.
class_root: The repository lacked one end-to-end invariant that a candidate remains isolated and hidden until the exact staged revision produces self-contained bytes that pass the shared bounded validator, after which Task1 promotion atomically switches model and mapping ownership while all temporary and network capabilities remain bounded.
affected_population: Users importing or editing any ComfyUI workflow while an older revision remains active
Users certifying video or audio whose path could change between probe and decode
Users importing GLB assets with external textures, dangling material references, or out-of-bounds accessors
Users calling provider multipart or custom-call routes that return oversized inline media responses
Users whose certification cleanup or Windows process-tree termination fails transiently
entry_points: ComfyUI workflow import and edit staging
Main-process exact candidate test execution and terminal result handling
Provider custom-call JSON and multipart responses
Certification finalization and delayed cleanup recovery

external_sources.purpose: Confirm protocol_whitelist semantics for restricting ffprobe and ffmpeg input protocols.
Confirm accessor, sparse accessor, bufferView, image, texture, material, and GLB self-containment constraints.

invariants: Every ComfyUI import or edit is an isolated disabled model and disabled mapping tagged with one opaque revision lease; normal catalog selection cannot execute it.
Only the main-process exact candidate resolver may execute a staged revision, and only when certifyOutput is explicit and revision, model, and task mapping all match.

The renderer retains the formal candidate vendorKey and revisionId returned by import or update, and the dedicated trusted IPC executes only that disabled revision; stale completions cannot clear a newer candidate.

Candidate identity is duplicated in a minimal trusted IPC envelope so grant, bridge, payload parsing, runtime loading, renderer destruction, window close, unmount, and revision replacement all cancel and fail only that exact staged lease; repeated cancellation is idempotent and promoted or newer revisions are untouched.

Successful unified media certification materializes matching bytes before Task1 promotion and persists one digest plus allowlisted metadata record per bounded asset; submit, poll, provider, materialization, certification, cancellation, and timeout failures delete only the exact staged lease and leave active rows byte-for-byte unchanged.
Certification digest, ffprobe, and ffmpeg decode consume the same held bytes; mutable temporary paths are materialization only and never security evidence.

GLB project writes accept only model/gltf-binary and reuse the shared no-DOM validator before persistence, including accessor bounds, sparse values, embedded image MIME and magic, and image-texture-material-mesh references.
ffprobe and ffmpeg accept only file, pipe, and data protocols, run under bounded process-tree teardown, and surface process_cleanup_failed without child output or paths.

A cleanup lease is atomically registered before provider bytes are written; per-root serialized manifest mutation preserves concurrent entries, skips fresh active runs, and reclaims stale crash leftovers without provider URLs or bodies.
Startup cleanup recovery schedules bounded retries whenever entries remain, so a fresh active lease is reclaimed automatically after its stale deadline even when no later certification runs.
Generated project media is rejected before disk unless MIME, magic, media kind, and real bounded decode agree or its exact byte digest matches trusted certification evidence.
Provider Adapter verification certifies every returned asset up to a hard count limit; any later HTML, oversize, corrupt, or wrong-kind asset prevents promotion.
Cross-origin redirects strip standard and declared credential headers, and credential-bearing requests reject redirects unless the caller explicitly opts in.
Multipart and custom-call transports use the same model-kind response budget as standard provider requests.
A bounded response-body deadline is preserved as timeout with response_timeout rather than being flattened into a generic network read failure.
migration: Existing active ComfyUI models remain active. New imports and edits create isolated candidates and switch only after certification. Existing assets remain readable; new GLB writes are validated. Cleanup recovery stores only opaque run directory names and removes the manifest after successful retry.
residual_risks: Non-seekable stdin may omit duration metadata for some valid audio containers; byte, process-time, stream-count, and real decode limits still apply, while known WAV duration is derived from its bounded RIFF header.
Textual glTF and externally referenced 3D resources remain unsupported until Nomi has a separately bounded resource package format.
